analysis:
The only change is a documentation edit in docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (head lines 170-174). It states that a lifecycle drain on a provider with no registered session completes without a coordinator acknowledgement once accepted work and local response writes finish (ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift, performLifecycleDrain). No code, wire fields, keys, or authorization logic change.

Security reading against the threat model: the passage is consistent with TB-002 and TB-011. A missing ack is already described as never implying success, and the barrier is not a bearer credential or permission to serve. The new sentence covers only the case where no session is registered, so there is no connection to fence and no coordinator-side billing barrier to wait for. Completion still waits for accepted inference work and local response writes, so it does not appear to permit dropping in-flight plaintext handling or encrypted-response writes. T-053 and T-008 are not affected.

One integration question remains outside the supplied evidence. The actual Swift behavior in performLifecycleDrain is not supplied, so I could not verify that the code matches the doc. In particular, I could not check that a stale or half-open session is not treated as no session, which could skip the coordinator barrier and its billing and settlement guarantee. Because this is a docs-only change, I report no finding. A reviewer of the Swift lifecycle code should confirm that the no-session predicate is strict and tied to the registered-session state.
